ImageDescription.value: Laura Secord (born Ingersoll, 13 September 1775 – 17 October 1868) was a Canadian heroine of the War of 1812. She is known for having walked 20 miles (32 km) out of American-occupied territory to warn British forces of an impending American attack. Her information led to the British victory at the Battle of Beaver Dams. Her contribution to the war was forgotten until 1860, when future king Albert Edward, Prince of Wales awarded the impoverished widow £100 for her service. Built in 1808 Laura lived here until 1835.

ImageDescription.value: The Christian Baptist church was built in 1874, in the original downtown core of Newmarket. The church began in 1822, and this structure was the third built for the Christian church denomination. The tower, with its large polygonal steeple, is centered in its Latin cross plan and is one of the oldest operating churches in Newmarket.

ImageDescription.value: We had made a pit stop in Niagara on the Lake where our guide had told us to go look for some breakfast for those who were interested. While setting us down, he had mentioned about a store called Just Christmas, which sells nothing else by Christmas decorations all the year round. Pictures of the store interior appear immediately after this, but I was wondering how they sustain their business for the rest of the year when demand is sure to be low! The probably depend on tourists and those passing through. (Niagara on the Lake, Ontario, Canada. Nov. 2015)
